_note: Figures somebody read off the running game, item by item. This file beats every other source: data/armory-stats.json is a bulk pull from a fan database and data/ballistics.json carries what a solver could derive, and both are a best guess at what the build does. A line in here is somebody looking at it. Nothing is written here by a script that fetches; it is typed, one reading at a time, through tools/measure.js.
_howToAdd: node tools/measure.js "<item name>" storage <W>x<H>, or kg, stack, rounds, grid, rpm, class, unlock. The examples carry no numbers on purpose: a usage line that looks like a real measurement gets run, and what it writes outranks every other source on the site. That happened once. The tool refuses a name that is not in data/armory.json, a value in a shape nothing reads, and the figures from the old examples.
_whatItDoes: The loadout page reads a measured figure in preference to a pulled one and says which it is using. On the damage page, a weapon that is listed as unfigured becomes a full row the moment it has both a measured rpm and a class whose damage rows cover its calibre, so measuring one number is all it takes to bring a weapon in.
